predecessors.note: Infobox: "Vassal state of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty (8th-10th century)", then "Sovereign monarchy (10th-12th century)"; the page dates neither the vassalage nor the independence.

successors.note: Vigraharaja IV took Delhi and Hansi in 1152; "The Tomaras continued to rule for a few more decades, but as vassals of the Chahamanas" (Vigraharaja IV page). The Tomara page itself says the Ghurid Muhammad of Ghor displaced the Chahamanas in 1192.

capitals.name: Anangpur
capitals.note: The Anangpal II page: "The first capital of the Tomar empire was Anangpur", no date; the span is a placeholder. [fx-36 H53, 1 Nov 2026: from moved 736 -> 885 with the state's start.]

capitals.name: Dhillika (Delhi)
capitals.note: "Anangpal Tomar founded Delhi in 1052" and the iron pillar was "fixed in Delhi in the year 1052"; the Tomara page puts the founding of Delhi in a footnote at 736. The 1052 date is used for the capital move.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Tomara row; the Chauhan Dynasty row covers the later Delhi region). The page says "the Tomaras ruled the Hariyanaka (Haryana) country before the Chahamanas" and built Dhillika; the Anangpal II page claims an empire "over various parts of Delhi, Haryana, Punjab" and five more states, undated and not drawn. Hansi and Thanesar changed hands with the Ghaznavids (1041-50) and are inside Haryana. No area on either page. [fx-36 H53, 1 Nov 2026: 'from' moved 736 -> 885 with the found (see ledger 0): the page's 736 is a footnote date citing Kulke and Rothermund, the earliest dated evidence is the Pehowa inscription of Mahendrapala I's reign (r. c. 885-910). The shape id keeps its old name.]

ledger.note: c. 885: the earliest evidence for the Tomaras. Tomara dynasty page: 'The earliest extant historical reference to the Tomaras occurs in the Pehowa inscription', 'issued during the reign of the Pratihara king Mahendrapala I (r. c. 885-910 CE)'; infobox 'Vassal state of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty (8th-10th century)'; 'As the Pratihara power declined, the Tomaras established a sovereign principality around Delhi by the 10th century'. The land is the Hariyanaka country and Dhillika (Haryana and Delhi), a Pratihara vassal at first. [fx-36 H53, 1 Nov 2026, from fx-33's handoff: the found was 736, which the page gives only in a footnote citing Kulke and Rothermund ('the Tomaras who had founded Delhi (Dhillika) in 736') beside the infobox 'c. 736-c. 1152', and the same page says 'much of the information about the dynasty comes from medieval bardic legends, which are not historically reliable'. 885 is the first year of the only dated evidence, the reign of Mahendrapala I; confidence 1. Haryana and Delhi stay with the Pratihara state until then. The page dates neither the vassalage nor the independence; no vassal event is booked here (see the handoff for data/hierarchy.csv).]

1041-1050 (bridge): Mahipala takes Hansi and Thanesar from the Ghaznavid Mawdud. the page gives Mawdud of Ghazni's reign as 1041-50 and says Mahipala captured Asigarh (Hansi) and Thaneshvara from him; the page gives no year for the capture, so 1041 is the start of Mawdud's reign.
1052: Anangpal II peoples Delhi. "In Samvat 1109 [1052 CE], [Anang] Pāl peopled Dilli."; the iron pillar was brought from Mathura and fixed there in the same year.

1152: Vigraharaja IV takes Delhi. "An old bahi (manuscript) states that Visaladeva i.e. Vigraharaja captured Delhi from Tamvars (Tomaras) in the year 1152 CE (1209 VS)"; the Bijolia inscription says he conquered Ashika (Hansi) and Delhi. The year rests on a manuscript, not an inscription.

1152: the Tomara state ends as a sovereign kingdom. "The Tomaras continued to rule for a few more decades, but as vassals of the Chahamanas" - the Chauhan dossier should carry the vassal tint (counterpart tomara-dynasty) to the 1192 Ghurid conquest.

wars.name: Tomara-Ghaznavid wars
wars.outcome: Mahipala captured Asigarh (Hansi) and Thaneshvara from Mawdud of Ghazni (r. 1041-50); Anangpal "defeated Turks led by Ibrahim Ghaznavi in Himachal pradesh", undated.
wars.note: Hansi had fallen to the Ghaznavids earlier (the page is silent on 1037); Anangpal II page is silent on 1038 Hansi and 1043 Lahore.

wars.name: Chahamana conquest of Delhi
wars.outcome: Vigraharaja IV (r. c. 1150-1164) captured Delhi and Hansi from the Tomaras in 1152 on the bahi's dating; the Tomaras survived as vassals.
wars.note: Dasharatha Sharma proposes the Tomaras had retaken Hansi from the Ghaznavids before Vigraharaja captured it.

certainty.note: No frontier is given on any page; only Haryana and Delhi are named.

notes: Cliopatria has no Tomara row. Three pages. The Tomara page gives 736 only in a footnote (fx-36 moved the start to c. 885, the Pehowa inscription under Mahendrapala I, r. c. 885-910; the bardic dates are 'not historically reliable') and contradicts the Anangpal II page (Delhi founded 1052); the infobox end 'c. 1152' agrees with the Vigraharaja IV page's 1152 (manuscript date), while the Chauhan dossier carries c. 1151 for the same event. The page says the Ghurid Muhammad of Ghor displaced the Chahamanas in 1192, so any Tomara vassal tint to 1192 belongs to the chauhan-dynasty dossier. Gazetteer names wanted: Anangpur, Dhillika, Hansi (Asigarh), Thanesar. The Mawdud-era gain is a bridge (page silent on the year).
